articles.title: Europe Diesel Demand Set to Trail Covid Levels in 2026

articles.title: OPEC Mulls Sticking with Current Quotas
articles.description: OPEC+ is considering rolling over current oil output quotas to January as it contends with uncertainties such as the impact of the Iran war, two delegates said.

articles.title: Eldridge Consortium Pens Deal to Acquire Lukoil International
articles.description: The agreement to acquire the sanctioned Russian company's upstream and downstream international assets aims to 'secure critical global energy assets under American and allied ownership', the consortium said.

articles.description: Part of Constellation's regulatory commitments related to its acquisition of Calpine, the sale to LS Power consisted of the Bethlehem, York 1 and York 2 facilities in Pennsylvania and Hay Road and Edge Moor in Delaware.

articles.description: Repsol and Eni have committed to invest $2bn over five years in Venezuelan ventures with state-owned PDVSA.

articles.title: Why Gasoline Prices Are Falling While Diesel Remains Expensive
articles.description: Americans heading into the Thanksgiving holiday are finally getting some relief at the gasoline pump. After months of elevated prices, the national average has fallen sharply in November, dropping to approximately $3.66 per gallon as of November 21. That’s a welcome development for millions of holiday travelers, although gasoline remains considerably more expensive than it was a year ago. articles.title: Tanker Traffic at Hormuz Ticks Up Despite Intensified Attacks
articles.description: The number of tankers carrying energy products through the Strait of Hormuz has increased in November despite the fact that the number of attacks and incidents with mines has hit the highest level since the beginning of the Iran war. Between November 1 and 19, the seven-day moving average count showed more than 26 crude oil, fuel, and LNG tankers transiting the Strait each day, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing ship-tracking data by Vortexa. articles.title: Why Copper's Thanksgiving Bounce May Not Be the Start of Anything
articles.description: Cross-asset sentiment is firmer on Thursday morning, with London copper prices up more than 3% from the lows on Wednseday. AI stocks rebounded yesterday following a US selloff, only to abruptly reverse course around noontime. With no obvious catalyst beyond a sharply weaker dollar, the move looks more like a relief rally driven by stretched positioning during a thin holiday trading week. articles.title: Ibom LNG appoints Afreximbank to advise on $1.5bn Nigeria LNG project
articles.description: Ibom LNG & Logistics Base has appointed the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) as financial adviser to support the mobilisation of $1.5bn for a proposed liquefied natural gas (LNG) facility in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria.

articles.title: Eldridge-led consortium to acquire Lukoil International assets
articles.description: A consortium led by US investment firm Eldridge has agreed to acquire Lukoil International (LIG), in a transaction that would shift ownership of the Russian group’s non-Russian oil and gas assets to American and allied hands.

articles.title: Cold Snap Squeezes UK Spare Power Capacity
articles.description: The UK faces a system margin shortfall of more than 2.7 gigawatts (GW) between noon and 8 p.m. local time on Thursday, as the cold snap is reducing the margin of spare capacity for the third day in a row. The UK’s National Energy System Operator (NESO) issued early on Thursday an electricity margin notice, which encourages market actions to increase system margins. Electricity Margin Notices are used to send a signal to the electricity market. It highlights that, in the short term, NESO would like a greater safety cushion,…

articles.title: Iranian Hardliners Call for Tanker Convoy to Defy U.S. Blockade
articles.description: With Iran's revenue from crude oil and condensate exports projected to hit zero by mid-December, hardline commentators and outlets close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) are increasingly advocating a direct challenge to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and waters. Their proposal is for a declared "convoy of tankers" to sail through the blockade, accompanied by threats to target the oil infrastructure of Iran's Gulf neighbors if US forces attack Iranian vessels. Iranian forces already attempted attacks on US targets in Bahrain…

articles.title: One Crew Member Dies as Diesel Tanker Sinks off Ibiza
articles.description: One crew member died as a tanker carrying diesel sank off the coast of Ibiza in the early hours on Thursday, local emergency services and authorities said. The Balearic Islands emergency service has activated an emergency plan after the diesel-carrying vessel sank about 25 nautical miles north of Ibiza, the emergency agency said on Thursday. Seven of the tanker’s 17 crew members were taken to Ibiza, but one of them was pronounced dead later in a hospital, the Balearic Islands emergency service announced. articles.title: Equinor cuts 2026 production guidance after shut-ins at three fields
articles.description: Equinor has revised its 2026 production growth guidance back to approximately 3%, reversing a recent upgrade, after temporary shut-ins and operational difficulties at three fields.

articles.title: Houthis Strike Saudi Ports on Red Sea
articles.description: Yemen's Houthis carried out strikes on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, as the Iran-backed militants and the kingdom continue to exchange fire with no signs of respite.

articles.title: Dutch Gas Network Operator Proposes Creation of Strategic Reserve
articles.description: Gasunie, the Dutch gas network operator, has urged the Netherlands to create a strategic gas reserve to boost energy security amid international supply disruptions. The Netherlands remains vulnerable to external supply shocks, Gasunie said on Thursday as gas demand for heating is soaring in an early cold spell in most of Europe this week. There is no immediate risk of supply shortage, but the country, as well as the whole of Europe, remains vulnerable to gas supply shocks, the company said. “Northwest Europe's gas infrastructure is currently…

articles.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Middle East Supply Fears Return
articles.description: January WTI crude oil futures recovered from a three-month low this week as renewed concern over Middle East supply brought buyers back into the market. Prices had fallen early in the week as traders focused on the prospect of a global surplus. The selling slowed after WTI reached $79.07, and the market rallied Wednesday after Yemen’s Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery. At 00:09 GMT Thursday, January WTI crude oil futures were trading at $84.01, up $0.60 or 0.72% for the week. The contract had traded as…

articles.title: Iran Says LNG Carrier Exploded After Hitting a Mine in Hormuz
articles.description: An LNG vessel has caught fire and exploded after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz during an attempt to transit on a route deemed “illegal” by Iran, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said in the latest communication of a tanker incident in the chokepoint. The LNG carrier had switched off its positioning systems and attempted to use “an unauthorized U.S.-Israeli-designated route,” the IRGC Navy’s Public Relations Office said, as carried by Iranian media early on Thursday. articles.title: Turkmenistan Nears Major Milestone in $10 Billion TAPI Gas Pipeline
articles.description: Turkmenistan expects a key section of a pipeline to begin supplying gas to Afghanistan’s third-largest city in early 2027, despite years of delays and hurdles in the $10-billion Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India (TAPI) project, Turkmen officials have told Reuters. Turkmenistan is estimated to be the world’s fifth-largest holder of natural gas reserves, after Russia, Iran, Qatar, and the United States. The Central Asian country holds an estimated 5.3% of global gas reserves, with 146 years of production at current…

articles.title: Japan’s Nuclear Revival Hits a Snag as TEPCO Delays Reactor Restart
articles.description: Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO) will delay the restart of a second reactor at its Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear power plant in Japan, the world’s largest in terms of nameplate capacity, after identifying a problem with the construction at the facility. TEPCO, which also operated the nuclear power plant in Fukushima prior to the 2011 disaster, has planned for years to restart the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa plant in the Niigata prefecture. articles.title: Libya Plans New Oil Bidding Rounds Despite Mounting Security Risks
articles.description: Libya has scheduled a bidding round for discovered but undeveloped oil fields in 2027, and another one in 2028 focused on exploration, as it seeks to ramp up oil production despite the unstable security situation. The National Oil Corporation last held a tender for undeveloped oil fields in 2025, the first in 18 years, and last year it awarded five of a total of 22 blocks on offer to companies including Chevron, Eni, Repsol, and QatarEnergy.
